newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. to push women's empowerment issues at summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to push women's empowerment issues at summit.

text.p: The United States will press for greater emphasis on linking women's rights and the environment at the United Nations Earth Summit, Under Secretary of State Tim Wirth said on Tuesday.

"There is not the kind of emphasis we would like to see" on women's issues in the document being negotiated this week at the U.N. summit, Wirth said at a panel discussion on population, women and the environment.

U.S. negotiators will try to get more language that addresses links between empowering women and fighting environmental degradation in the document that is to emerge from the five-day summit, he said.

The Netherlands U.N. ambassador, Nicolaas Biegman, said the issue of empowering women was more controversial at the last Earth Summit five years ago in Rio de Janeiro, and so there was little reference to it in that summit's agreement.
"Now it is difficult to insert it in this document," Biegman said.

Nafis Sadik, executive director of the United Nations Population Fund, said a wider understanding was needed "of these life-sustaining synergies -- women's empowerment, gender concerns, population pressures, poverty, environmental degradation and sustainable development."
